email.subject1: a signal play for Higher Logic
email.body1:
Wyatt, saw Higher Logic launched its Vanilla MCP server and brought on a new Chief Community Officer to push AI-powered engagement.

New capabilities like that flood the funnel with signals faster than they can be turned into action. Our AI SDR closes that signal-to-action latency, researching, writing, and following up autonomously: 3-5x more meetings per rep, no new hires.

I built a personalized signal play for Higher Logic off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them tend to progress about 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Wyatt, quick follow-up for Higher Logic.

Shipping AI capabilities usually means cross-sell and expansion signals stacking up faster than reps can act. As RevOps, you feel that latency first, and it's hard to show measurable lift when follow-up is the bottleneck.

Want 15 minutes? I'll walk you through a teardown of your current outbound, three things I'd change. Our best practices alone usually lift response rates 50 to 70 percent.
email.body3:
Wyatt, last bit of proof for Higher Logic.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and couldn't hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks with every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how Higher Logic's reply rate likely compares to other community software teams. Want to hop on a quick call and I'll walk you through it?
email.body4:
Wyatt, I'll stop reaching out on this one, but didn't want to leave you empty-handed.

If tightening signal-to-action without adding headcount isn't a priority right now, no problem at all. Timing is everything while new capabilities roll out, and that stretch is its own kind of busy.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to a RevOps motion? I'll tailor it to Higher Logic either way.
